transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-07
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM); Carlos Mendez (Apex VP Eng), Rashida Khan (Apex SRE), Tom Berger (Apex Head of ML), Leah Park (Apex Procurement)

Summary: quick renewal & expansion check. Apex considering extending contract 12->24 months, adding two regions (eu-west, ap-southeast), and moving part of workload to Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput. Discussed pricing, SLA impacts, burst capacity, and procurement timeline.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you all making time. quick round robin — if you could just say your name and role.
[00:12] Carlos Mendez: yeah hi it's carlos, vp engineering at apex.
[00:15] Rashida Khan: rashida, i'm s r e, tuning infra and observability.
[00:18] Tom Berger: tom, head of ml, i own the models and inference pipelines.
[00:22] Leah Park: leah from procurement.
[00:24] Maya Chen: great, and from redwood we have liam and priya, liam do you want to give a quick agenda?
[00:30] Liam Ortiz: sure, uh, agenda: renewal timing and term options, capacity options (dedicated vs hosted), multi-region rollout and network concerns, price and discounts, and next steps — we'll leave time for q&a.
[00:40] Tom Berger: sounds good. quick context: we've been on hosted for 14 months, spiking at peak hours; the team's looking to guarantee latency for customer-facing features, and we want to go into eu and apac in q3.
[00:52] Maya Chen: got it, thank you. rashida, can you summarize the infra constraints?
[00:56] Rashida Khan: yeah so main thing is we have strict egress rules, v p c peering requirements with our cloud accounts, and we'd want KMS integration for key management; also, around traffic shape: most requests are bursty — mornings in us-east then evenings europe — so a mix of sustained and burst.
[01:15] Liam Ortiz: that jives with what we saw in the logs you shared. for the latency targets, what's your p95/p99 target right now for the user-facing endpoints?
[01:23] Carlos Mendez: p95 we want under 350ms, p99 under 800ms ideally. right now on hosted we're at about 420/1.1s at peak, so that's why dedicated is on the table.
[01:34] Liam Ortiz: okay, good. dedicated typically gets you more predictable p95s because you control GPU pools, batching windows, and you can pin model variants. you mentioned multi-region — do you want active-active, or active-primary with read replicas?
[01:46] Tom Berger: prefer active-primary to start, low-lift, then move to active-active once we validate cross-region caching behavior.
[01:52] Maya Chen: makes sense. for active-primary we can place Dedicated in us-east and add read capacity in eu-west and ap-southeast as cold replicas, or use routing policy to send eu traffic to eu cluster — that will add some replication complexity though.
[02:06] Rashida Khan: two questions: one, how does KV cache replicate across regions? and two, does dedicated support our KMS/HSM setup?
[02:14] Liam Ortiz: good questions. kv cache is local to the serving cluster — we can replicate prefixes asynchronously but there's a consistency tradeoff. in practice for low-latency user queries we recommend per-region warm caches and a short TTL, so you avoid cross-region fetches. and on k m s, our private offering supports customer-managed keys via standard km s integrations, we can show the network diagrams.
[02:36] Tom Berger: ok. regarding cost: if we move to dedicated and add two regions, what's the delta on committed spend?
[02:42] Maya Chen: at a high level, the committed capacity is driven by GPU pool size and the reservation term. for example, a 3x A100-like pool in us-east to cover peak would be X, adding eu-west read pool and ap-southeast read pool smaller at Y each — i'll send the exact line items after this. we also have an autoscale burst option so you don't have to reserve full peak in region, you can reserve baseline and allow burst to hosted with fallback.
[03:04] Leah Park: procurement will want a clear line on: committed monthly fee, overage rates, and SLAs. any chance to get a contract amendment template?
[03:12] Priya Desai: yes we can provide a redlined amendment showing term extension, regional add-ons, and the dedicated reserved capacity terms. we'll attach SLA metrics and credits.
[03:20] Carlos Mendez: how do you price burst usage that falls back to hosted? we've seen spiky bursts where cost balloons.
[03:27] Liam Ortiz: burst-to-hosted is metered differently — there's a per-token compute surcharge plus provision for cold-start overhead. we usually model expected monthly cost using your token distribution — that's why we asked for hourly token histograms.
[03:37] Rashida Khan: we'll share that, yes. one other thing: can you run a quick perf baseline on our workloads? we have long context windows up to 8k tokens for some queries.
[03:46] Liam Ortiz: absolutely, we can run a benchmark. we'll need sample prompts and typical sequence lengths. for 8k contexts quantization and kv cache behaviors are important — sometimes you see throughput drop if kv caching isn't tuned for long contexts.
[03:58] Tom Berger: are there model variants we should consider? we've been using a 13B open model; wondering if a quantized 30B variant would be better for quality but price tradeoffs.
[04:08] Maya Chen: yes— tradeoffs. 30B quantized might give better quality but require different memory profile. our Optimize team can recommend quantization profiles; sometimes better to keep 13B and tune prompts for lower cost. we'll pair you with recommendations.
[04:20] Leah Park: timeline — procurement needs to finalize by end of May to hit July rollout. is that feasible?
[04:26] Maya Chen: yes with a 24-month renewal and committed capacity agreement we can target July. we need signed amendment by May 28 to start provisioning and cross-region capacity testing in June.
[04:36] Carlos Mendez: okay that works. questions on security: does Redwood provide audit logs and per-request metadata for compliance?
[04:42] Priya Desai: yes we provide audit logs, token-level usage, request/response traces (scrubbed if requested), and support SSO/SAML, SCIM for user provisioning. there is an add-on for extended log retention.
[04:56] Rashida Khan: good. for VPC peering, will you need inbound rules on our side or will the redwood private agent connect outbound?
[05:03] Liam Ortiz: for Private deployments we usually do customer outbound connections to our control plane and a customer-managed data plane inside the VPC; for Dedicated hosted we do peering — we'll share the network diagrams.
[05:14] Tom Berger: the team also wanted a demo of model rollouts and canary fallback. can you show a quick screenshot or is that a separate session?
[05:20] Maya Chen: we can demo next week; for today we can walk through the policy at a high level. our rollout supports canary percentages, auto-rollbacks when error or latency regressions exceed thresholds, and automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if GPUs are constrained.
[05:36] Leah Park: about discounts — what kind of tiering for 24-months vs 12-months?
[05:40] Maya Chen: typically a term discount of 8-12% for 24 months vs 12, plus volume discounts for committed token throughput. we'll model both options in the quote.
[05:49] Carlos Mendez: can you include an option that keeps retention and logging add-ons for HIPAA workloads? we may have partners requiring that.
[05:55] Priya Desai: yes, we have a compliance pack for HIPAA with extended retention, extra audit controls, and business associate agreement — we'll include that option.
[06:03] Rashida Khan: ok, a couple of technical nitpicks: how do you handle KV eviction when cache pressure mounts, and is that something we can tune per-route?
[06:12] Liam Ortiz: eviction is LRU-ish but we expose policies per-route: TTL, max entries, and cold-fetch behavior. for high-throughput endpoints you can pin small warm caches to avoid remote fetches.
[06:25] Carlos Mendez: if we do dedicated, how long to provision a new region? assuming capacity available.
[06:31] Maya Chen: typical provisioning lead time is 4-6 weeks to stand up dedicated pools and validate networking, but we can accelerate with a committed start date and pre-provisioning options — we offered burst capacity as an intermediate step.
[06:45] Tom Berger: are there any constraints for GPU types? we've historically used A100 but are evaluating H100 in the future.
[06:52] Liam Ortiz: we support multiple instance families; we can map model profiles to GPU types. H100 gives better throughput for large models but also different kernel behavior; our runtime will select kernels accordingly. we'll include model-GPU pairing guidance.
[07:06] Leah Park: procurement question: do you accept PO and net-45?
[07:09] Maya Chen: yes we accept PO and net terms; for enterprise a typical path is PO + signed amendment + upfront or monthly billing depending on contract. finance prefers net-30 but we can discuss net-45.
[07:19] Rashida Khan: circling back to fallback: if dedicated is saturated and you fallback to hosted, do you guarantee model parity? we've seen fallbacks sometimes change quality.
[07:29] Priya Desai: fallback will route to the same model family; there can be variance if the host uses a quantized variant, so we recommend validating the fallback variant with a holdout prompt set — we can run regression tests and add quality guards to the rollout policy.
[07:45] Carlos Mendez: ok, that helps. any red flags on compliance for us moving to dedicated + private?
[07:51] Maya Chen: nothing major; we'll provide the SOC 2 report, network diagram, and the BAA if needed. for private/on-prem there are more docs but the core items are KMS, audit logs, and access controls.
[08:03] Tom Berger: can you include notes about evals and quality monitoring? we want alerting on model drift and regression on key prompts.
[08:10] Liam Ortiz: yes, Redwood Optimize ties into quality monitoring — you can upload prompt sets and we run automated evals, and trigger alerts if regression crosses thresholds. we'll include that as a recommended add-on.
[08:23] Maya Chen: ok let's recap next steps and owners: we'll send a revised quote for 24-months with dedicated baseline in us-east and read pools in eu-west and ap-southeast; include burst-to-hosted pricing, SLA and amendment template, SOC2/network diagrams, and a proposed capacity-sizing workshop.
[08:38] Leah Park: procurement will review the amendment, please include standard termination clauses and notice periods.
[08:44] Maya Chen: will do. rashida and tom will share perf samples and hourly token histograms; liam will run a baseline benchmark and sizing doc; maya will send pricing. agreed timeline: signed amendment by 2027-05-28 to hit July provisioning.
[08:59] Carlos Mendez: sounds good. anything else?
[09:02] Tom Berger: one last thing — can you also include an option to add on a third region if needed down the line and pre-agree on the provisioning ramp?
[09:10] Maya Chen: yes we'll add a reserved-option clause for future regions.
[09:14] Leah Park: thanks everyone.
[09:16] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in writing with the attachments.

End of call.
